label: give an opinion or an evaluation
note: Chapter 89, AND THE OLD NOTE WAS SUBSTANTIALLY WRONG, which is worth recording because it made this look like the most expensive point in the file. It said 'I think that ... needs ennu plus cintikkuka' as though neither existed. BOTH ARE TAUGHT. ennu is chapter 72's quoting marker and cintikkuka is chapter 33's verb, and ML-C72-ennu-more already pairs them explicitly -- its worked example is literally 'enikku malayaalam ariyaam' ennu njaan cintikkunnu, 'I think I know Malayalam'. So the assembly the point asks for was on the page before this chapter was written. What was genuinely missing was only the EVALUATION VOCABULARY, and that half of the note was right: nallathu and mosham both returned ZERO files. The chapter therefore teaches TWO WORDS AND NO GRAMMAR. It spends its first lesson on -athu, which lets a quality stand without a noun to lean on (nalla needs one, nallathu does not) and which is visibly the word athu, 'that', so nallathu is 'the that-which-is-good'; it works on all five taught qualities with no exceptions. The second teaches mosham, filling a real hole -- five qualities and not one of them negative meant half of every opinion was unsayable. The third only assembles: atu nallathaanu ennu njaan cintikkunnu. The lesson says so plainly, because it is the interesting part: the machinery was in place before there was anything worth carrying with it.
